title: Final 19 zero-evidence programs — primary research committee handoff
objective: Fresh external primary-source research on the 19 genuine zero-evidence residual programs (docs/validation/GLOBAL_ECONOMIC_DATA_ZERO_EVIDENCE_21.json minus the 2 already resolved: on_ofttc, ocase). NO implementation performed -- this artifact is the handoff to independent Codex/Gemini committee review before any canonicalization.

denominator.population_source: docs/validation/GLOBAL_ECONOMIC_DATA_ZERO_EVIDENCE_21.json (21 named programs) minus 2 already RESOLVED (on_ofttc, ocase) = 19

accounting_84_reconciliation.summary: Mechanically traced via git history and JSON artifact diffing. Conclusion: the exact missing 84th identity is NOT recoverable, and is very likely NOT a real missing program -- it is population drift from computing len(BLOCKED_SLUGS)-style counts against a live, continuously-edited coverage registry at different commits, filtered to a 'formulaic_total' classification that was never itself persisted as a literal name list anywhere in the repo.
trace: docs/validation/GLOBAL_BASE_PRICEABILITY_CLOSEOUT.json (commit 8c31418): formulaic_total=126, priced_before=31, priced_after=32, economic_input_genuinely_missing=94 -- the ORIGIN of the '94' figure. Its own genuinely_missing_economic_inputs.count=94 is a bare integer with NO literal name list attached (meaning field only, no 'programs' array).

docs/validation/GLOBAL_ECONOMIC_DATA_BASE_PRICING_CLOSEOUT.json (commit 9f7c5cf): formulaic_total=126, priced_before=32 (matches prior priced_after), priced_after=42 (confirms 10 resolved in between -- 'already-Georgia-class-resolved', matching the denominator_reconciliation_note's '94 minus 10 = 84'), genuinely_missing_economic_input=84. This artifact DOES name 62 of the 84 explicitly (next_batch_candidates_with_existing_parsed_data) -- the remaining 22 were never individually listed here either, only implied by the count.

docs/validation/GLOBAL_ECONOMIC_DATA_ZERO_EVIDENCE_21.json (commit 34b4783): derives its 21 Path-B programs from a DIFFERENT stated basis ('94 originally blocked formulaic programs MINUS 73 with cited PARSED-tier historical data = 21'), using 94 and 73 directly rather than 84 and 62 -- a second, inconsistent accounting basis appears at this point (73 != 62), suggesting the Path-A/Path-B split was recomputed against the registry's THEN-current state rather than reconciled against the original 84-artifact's own 62-name list.

Attempted direct set-difference: extracted the literal BLOCKED_SLUGS at commit 8c31418 via `git show` + regex parse of authority_coverage_registry.py's _ROWS tuple. Result: 245 total blocked slugs at that commit (spanning ALL blocking states -- UNPRICEABLE_AUTHORITY_INSUFFICIENT, NON_GUARANTEED_SELECTIVE, NON_ECONOMIC, NO_CURRENT_INCENTIVE, SUPERSEDED, DUPLICATE, CANONICAL_DATA_HANDOFF_DEFECT), not 94 or 126. This confirms the 94/126 figures were filtered to a narrower 'formulaic classification' universe that has never existed as a standalone persisted list -- there is no artifact in this repository's history, at any commit, that names all 84 (or 94, or 126) programs literally. The count was always a live, point-in-time derived number.
accounting_84_reconciliation.conclusion: The historical 84 count is very likely internally consistent at the moment it was computed but is not independently reconstructable to an exact named list with the tools available (no snapshot of the 'formulaic_total=126' classification exists as literal names at that commit). This is a genuine, disclosed pre-existing gap in this project's own record-keeping discipline -- not evidence of a hidden/lost program, and not something this task's own denominator depends on: the 19-program population for THIS task is independently and directly enumerable from GLOBAL_ECONOMIC_DATA_ZERO_EVIDENCE_21.json (21 minus 2 resolved = 19), verified by direct enumeration in Phase A below, with zero ambiguity.

programs.program_name: INCAA (Instituto Nacional de Cine y Artes Audiovisuales) -- as originally scoped

Reported rate: up to 25% cash rebate on eligible local spend, cap ARS 440 million per project, minimum eligible spend ARS 200 million, minimum 4 filming days in the City. minimum eligible spend ARS 200 million

programs.program_name: Screen NSW Production Finance Fund (and related Made in NSW / Regional Filming Fund streams)

economic_propositions.rate_formula: Calculated as a percentage of Qualifying NSW Production Expenditure (QNSWPE); Made in NSW TV Drama stream: up to 10% of Qualifying NSW Spend, capped at $1M. Documentary/Factual: up to 10% of QNSWPE. Regional Filming Fund: up to 10% of budgeted QRPE, capped at $200,000. Main Production Finance Fund: percentage of QNSWPE, capped at $850,000 per project.
economic_propositions.qpe_basis: Qualifying NSW Production Expenditure (QNSWPE) / Qualifying NSW Spend / Qualifying Regional Production Expenditure (QRPE), stream-dependent
economic_propositions.cap: $850,000 (Production Finance Fund) / $1,000,000 (Made in NSW TV Drama) / $200,000 (Regional Filming Fund) -- stream-dependent
economic_propositions.monetization: grant (not a tax credit or rebate)
economic_propositions.other: Assessed against merit criteria including an explicit 'Contribution to diversity (10%)' scoring weight -- confirms competitive/discretionary assessment, not automatic entitlement.

requirements: Merit-based application, assessed by Screen NSW against published criteria (including diversity contribution)

source_provenance.citation_detail: Official screen.nsw.gov.au and content.screen.nsw.gov.au URLs identified and confirmed to exist via search; direct WebFetch of both the HTML page (403) and the PDF guidelines (403) were blocked. Figures corroborated via search-engine snippets that directly quote the guidelines document (grants.com.au, Avant Group, Digby Law industry-update commentary).

programs.interpretation_notes: This is a competitive grant program with published assessment criteria, explicitly NOT a guaranteed formulaic rebate -- distinct in character from the federal Location Offset (au_location_offset), which IS a guaranteed statutory rebate. Do not conflate the two.
open_questions: Official screen.nsw.gov.au domain returned 403 on direct WebFetch both for the HTML page and the PDF guidelines -- primary-source text not directly quoted; figures are PARSED-tier via convergent secondary corroboration only.
programs.proposed_canonical_treatment: SELECTIVE_DISCRETIONARY / GRANT_FUND -- preserve for later optimizer/grants-fund restoration; do not model as a deterministic base-pricing rate.

programs.program_name: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
programs.current_status: RESEARCHED -- well-established, high-confidence, direct primary fetch blocked but extremely well-corroborated

economic_propositions.qpe_basis: Qualified labour expenditure, capped at not more than 60% of production costs net of assistance
economic_propositions.cap: No stated dollar cap on the credit amount itself (only the 60%-of-production-cost labour-expenditure ceiling)
economic_propositions.payroll_treatment: Credit base is qualified LABOUR expenditure specifically, not all-spend
economic_propositions.other: Distinct from ca_federal_pstc (Production Services Tax Credit, already canonical, no Canadian-content requirement) -- CPTC is the Canadian-content-certified parallel credit, structurally analogous to the CA-ON OFTTC/OPSTC split already modeled.

requirements: CAVCO Canadian-content certification (points test)
eligible Canadian production company

source_provenance.issuing_authority: Canadian Audio-Visual Certification Office (CAVCO), jointly with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)

programs.interpretation_notes: High confidence despite the direct-fetch block -- the 25%/60%-labour-cap structure has been stable and consistently reported since program inception (1995) across every source consulted.

programs.program_name: Ffilm Cymru Wales Feature Film Production Fund
programs.current_status: RESEARCHED -- confirmed discretionary co-investment grant with a Wales-talent eligibility gate materially different from a general international incentive

economic_propositions.rate_formula: Up to £600,000 (most awards £150,000-£400,000); investment not to exceed 50% of the project's budget
economic_propositions.monetization: grant (National Lottery via Arts Council of Wales + Welsh Government funds via Creative Wales), not equity investment
economic_propositions.other: MATERIAL ELIGIBILITY GATE: requires 'Wales born or based talent in the lead writer, producer and/or director role' -- this is not a general international-production attraction incentive; it is a Wales-talent-development fund. A foreign production relocating to Wales without Wales-affiliated key creatives would likely not qualify at all.

requirements: Wales-born or Wales-based lead writer, director, and/or producer
Board review at scheduled meetings (not competitive rounds) for awards of £50,000+

source_provenance.issuing_authority: Ffilm Cymru Wales, funded via Arts Council of Wales (National Lottery) and Creative Wales (Welsh Government)
source_provenance.citation_detail: Direct WebFetch succeeded and returned exact figures: 'up to a maximum of £600,000, but most awards will be in the £150,000 - £400,000 range', 'our investment not to exceed 50% of your budget', the Wales-talent eligibility requirement, and Board-review process, all quoted directly.

programs.interpretation_notes: The Wales-talent gate is the single most important finding here -- this program is materially DIFFERENT in character from what the original artifact scoped ('Wales Screen Production Fund... for international productions'). It is a homegrown-talent development fund, not a general relocation incentive. Flag for committee: does a canonical_program_id under this name even belong in the base-pricing worldwide catalog at all, or is it out of scope by design (similar to official co-production mechanisms)?
open_questions: Is there a SEPARATE, general Wales production incentive without the talent-nationality gate that better matches the original scoping intent? Not found in this research pass -- AVEC (UK-wide) is the closest general mechanism available to a Wales-based international shoot.

programs.program_name: Jamaica film industry incentives (JAMPRO-administered: Employment Tax Credit, bond waivers, duty relief, case-by-case Production Rebates)
programs.current_status: RESEARCHED -- confirmed to lack a fixed deterministic rate for foreign productions

economic_propositions.monetization: Mixed: (1) Employment Tax Credit up to 30% of LOCAL companies' PAYE tax obligations (payroll-tax offset, not a direct production QPE rebate); (2) duty-free importation / bond waivers on production equipment (in-kind, not cash); (3) 'Production Rebates' explicitly evaluated case-by-case with rolling JAMPRO acceptance, 'funded where the decision is favourable' -- confirmed discretionary, not automatic.

local production partner (for Production Rebates)

programs.program_name: RIPAC (under the SCRI.PT programme) -- Portugal's consolidated film/audiovisual production incentive, administered by ICA
